subject: GEO
name: Georgia
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. claims.title: Kingdom of Colchis flourishes
claims.summary: On the Black Sea coast of western Georgia, the wealthy kingdom of Colchis, the land of the Golden Fleece in Greek myth, traded with the Greek world and developed a society famed for its metalwork.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-600bce-kingdom-of-colchis-flourishes, claim TL:GEO:event:600bce:kingdom-of-colchis-flourishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdom of Iberia founded
claims.summary: The eastern Georgian kingdom of Iberia emerged in the lands of Kartli, centred on Mtskheta, forming a distinct monarchy that would become the core of the Georgian state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-300bce-kingdom-of-iberia-founded, claim TL:GEO:event:300bce:kingdom-of-iberia-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pompey campaigns in the Caucasus
claims.summary: The Roman general Pompey campaigned in Colchis and Iberia, drawing the Georgian lands into the long contest between Rome and the Iranian empires over the Caucasus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-65bce-pompey-campaigns-in-the-caucasus, claim TL:GEO:event:65bce:pompey-campaigns-in-the-caucasus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iberia adopts Christianity
claims.summary: Through the preaching of St Nino, King Mirian III of Iberia adopted Christianity as the state religion, making Georgia one of the world's oldest Christian states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-337-iberia-adopts-christianity, claim TL:GEO:event:337:iberia-adopts-christianity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab conquest and the Emirate of Tbilisi
claims.summary: Arab armies brought Islam to the Caucasus and established an emirate at Tbilisi, beginning centuries in which Georgian princely houses contested Muslim and Byzantine power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-645-arab-conquest-and-the-emirate-of-tbilisi, claim TL:GEO:event:645:arab-conquest-and-the-emirate-of-tbilisi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bagrat III unites Georgia
claims.summary: Bagrat III of the Bagrationi dynasty united the eastern and western Georgian lands into a single kingdom, laying the foundation for the medieval golden age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1008-bagrat-iii-unites-georgia, claim TL:GEO:event:1008:bagrat-iii-unites-georgia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Didgori
claims.summary: David IV the Builder defeated a much larger Seljuk Turkish coalition at Didgori west of Tbilisi, a decisive victory that broke Seljuk power in the Caucasus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1121-battle-of-didgori, claim TL:GEO:event:1121:battle-of-didgori, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tbilisi recovered and made capital
claims.summary: David IV recaptured Tbilisi from Muslim rule, ending centuries of the emirate and establishing the city as the royal capital of a reunited Georgia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1122-tbilisi-recovered-and-made-capital, claim TL:GEO:event:1122:tbilisi-recovered-and-made-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Queen Tamar
claims.summary: Tamar, titled mepe ('king'), brought Georgia to the height of its power and prestige, ruling a pan-Caucasian realm and presiding over a cultural golden age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1184-reign-of-queen-tamar, claim TL:GEO:event:1184:reign-of-queen-tamar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rustaveli's national epic
claims.summary: Shota Rustaveli composed 'The Knight in the Panther's Skin', the Georgian national epic, the supreme literary achievement of the golden age and a classic of world literature.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1200-rustaveli-s-national-epic, claim TL:GEO:event:1200:rustaveli-s-national-epic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Invasions of Timur
claims.summary: The armies of Timur (Tamerlane) repeatedly devastated Georgia, accelerating the breakup of the kingdom into rival principalities amid Mongol and Turkic pressure.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1386-invasions-of-timur, claim TL:GEO:event:1386:invasions-of-timur, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Georgievsk
claims.summary: King Erekle II of Kartli-Kakheti placed his kingdom under Russian protection, ceding control of foreign affairs in exchange for guarantees of its integrity and dynasty against Persia and the Ottomans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1783-treaty-of-georgievsk, claim TL:GEO:event:1783:treaty-of-georgievsk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russia annexes Kartli-Kakheti
claims.summary: The Russian Empire unilaterally annexed eastern Georgia and abolished the Bagrationi monarchy, beginning the absorption of the Georgian lands that was completed over the following decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1801-russia-annexes-kartli-kakheti, claim TL:GEO:event:1801:russia-annexes-kartli-kakheti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Democratic Republic of Georgia proclaimed
claims.summary: Amid the collapse of the Russian Empire, Georgia proclaimed an independent democratic republic governed by Mensheviks, with a democratic constitution and land reform.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1918-democratic-republic-of-georgia-proclaimed, claim TL:GEO:event:1918:democratic-republic-of-georgia-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Red Army conquest
claims.summary: The Soviet Red Army invaded, took Tbilisi after heavy fighting and proclaimed the Georgian SSR on 25 February 1921, incorporating Georgia into the Soviet Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1921-red-army-conquest, claim TL:GEO:event:1921:red-army-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The April 9 tragedy in Tbilisi
claims.summary: Soviet troops violently broke up a peaceful pro-independence demonstration in Tbilisi, killing about twenty people and galvanising the Georgian national movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1989-the-april-9-tragedy-in-tbilisi, claim TL:GEO:event:1989:the-april-9-tragedy-in-tbilisi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence restored
claims.summary: Following a referendum on 31 March, the Supreme Council adopted the Act restoring Georgia's independence on 9 April 1991, two years after the April 9 tragedy.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country: Georgia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1991-independence-restored, claim TL:GEO:event:1991:independence-restored, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War in Abkhazia
claims.summary: Fighting between Georgian forces and Abkhaz separatists, with outside support, ended in Georgian defeat and the displacement of much of the ethnic Georgian population; casualty figures are disputed estimates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-1992-war-in-abkhazia, claim TL:GEO:event:1992:war-in-abkhazia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Rose Revolution
claims.summary: Peaceful mass protests over disputed elections, in which demonstrators carried roses, forced the resignation of President Shevardnadze and brought the reformer Mikheil Saakashvili to power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-2003-the-rose-revolution, claim TL:GEO:event:2003:the-rose-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russia–Georgia war over South Ossetia
claims.summary: A five-day war around South Ossetia drew in the Russian military; estimates put the combined dead at about 850 with over 100,000 displaced. Russia then recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia, a step most states rejected.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Georgia: From the land of the Golden Fleece to a Caucasian crossroads facing west.", terralore.co/country/GEO/chronicle#ev-2008-russia-georgia-war-over-south-ossetia, claim TL:GEO:event:2008:russia-georgia-war-over-south-ossetia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: EU Association Agreement
claims.summary: Georgia signed an Association Agreement with the European Union, deepening a Western orientation that later led to its 2022 EU membership application and 2023 candidate status.
